Trading Rules
Hedging is Prohibited
Hedging is Prohibited

Hedging is Prohibited

Updated this week
This policy means you cannot use multiple trading accounts to offset risk by placing opposite trades across them. The firm considers that a way of manipulating its evaluation or funded-account rules.
Simple examples

Trading setup

	

Allowed?




Account 1: Long NQ; Account 2: Short NQ

	

❌ No




Your account: Long ES; another account: Short ES

	

❌ No




Same account: Long a mini contract and short its micro equivalent

	

✅ According to the policy, yes




Same account: Long ES and short NQ

	

✅ According to the policy, yes




Different accounts: One long gold, another short gold

	

❌ No

What happens if you hedge?

First offense: You may receive an email warning, and the involved accounts can be closed.

If done in a Buffer or Sim Funded account, you may forfeit the account and any payouts.

Repeated offenses: You may be permanently banned from the firm

What does this mean for you in practice?

You should avoid opening opposing positions across separate accounts, even if:

Your intention is to reduce risk rather than manipulate the evaluation.

This rule applies to All User and Same Household Accounts.
